title: Directional and multi-target strategies to confirm a high-energy recoil population: what a 250 keV recoil track would look like and who could see it
question: Which directional targets (F, He, S, C, O, Ca, Br, Ag, I, Xe, W in gas TPCs, emulsions, crystals) can scatter for the LZ-favoured inelastic (delta 300-380 keV) and elastic L10 interpretations, what recoil-direction distributions and 3 sigma event counts follow for a 30 deg / 70 % head-tail detector, where would the 16 June recoil have pointed at SURF, and how does direction fit the multi-target confirmation programme?
headline_result: Inelastic 248 keV recoils near the kinematic ceiling are collinear with the DM wind (all within 21 deg of the anti-apex at delta = 366 keV; 3-5 ideal events for 3 sigma, 23-30 with 30 deg resolution and 70 % head-tail), but every F/He/S/C/O directional detector is kinematically blind (ceilings 14-131 keV), Ag emulsions stop at 333 keV, and heavy-gas TPCs collect < 1 event/yr per 1000 m3 at LZ's rate (Xe 40 Torr: 246/111/41/6 yr to 3 sigma for delta = 300/350/366/380; fluorine L10: 2700 yr): direction cannot confirm the hint before xenon counting, isotopes and tungsten do
key_numbers: ceilings (1 TeV, June) He 14, C 40, O 54, F 63, S 106, Ca 131, Br 253, Ag 333, I 386, Xe 398, W 533 keV; A_min 96/114/120/125 (delta 300/350/366/380); F elastic end-point 249 keV; thetaR_max(Xe 248 keV) 65/30/19/14.5/8 deg; <cos gamma> 0.59/0.89/0.95/0.97/0.99, F L10 0.70; N_3sigma obs 30/25/24/23 inelastic, 50 F L10, 69 Xe elastic, ideal 3-9, axial 4.6; SURF apex RA 319.4 Dec +43.7 alt -0.5 az 347; recoil alt +1 (-13..+14) az 167+-11 (delta 366), +-49 elastic; apex below horizon 11 % of the day; tracks at 250 keV F/CF4 4 mm, Xe gas 1.5 mm, I/CF3I 1.0 mm, Ag 0.2 um, LXe 0.15 um; rates F 0.146/t yr, Xe gas 1000 m3 0.12/0.22/0.60/3.6 per yr, Ag emulsion 1.9e-3 per 100 kg yr; L10 unit coupling 3.32 LZ events (P012 3.34)
model_or_mechanism: two-body recoil kinematics (cos thetaR = vmin/v) and Radon transform of the Baxter-2021 truncated Maxwellian boosted to the lab (astropy ephemeris, 16 June 2023) by importance-sampled Monte Carlo; WimPyDD L10 (q^2 O4 - O6) and inelastic O1 kernels on 19F and Xe via a flat-halo trick; Gaussian dipole/FB/axial anisotropy statistics with toy validation; analytic GMST horizon transform; recalled SRIM-scale track lengths
